item.evidence: backend/routes_orders.py:127-132 defines expiry cleanup; its callers are checkout (:158) and backend/routes_admin.py:63,89,176. backend/routes_store.py:36-60 reads stock without cleanup; backend/server.py:44-48 schedules only index creation and seeds, not expiry.
item.expected: R-101: "the 15-minute expiry of an unpaid reservation ... return the reserved quantity ... GET /api/products/{id} afterwards shows the pre-checkout stock". After an unpaid last-unit reservation expires, stock should be available to browsing shoppers without an unrelated action.

After 15 minutes, a shopper merely reloading the last-unit product still sees stock 0 and cannot add it. The stored reservation has no independently running expiry. An admin visit or another checkout can recover it, but ordinary browsing cannot.

Close the browser without dismissing Razorpay, so abandon is never called.
Wait over 15 minutes without other checkouts or admin requests.

item.evidence: backend/routes_orders.py:91-96 first writes status placed, payment.status paid and stock_reserved True; only :99-105 then attempts to reserve expired stock and potentially overwrites the order to cancelled. backend/routes_admin.py:98-102 accepts any paid order; :127-140 can cancel the exposed placed order and unconditionally return its quantities. :79 allows packing a placed order.
item.expected: R-102: "re-reserves the stock when it is still available" or records paid-awaiting-refund when unavailable; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Multi-document operations leave no half-written state on failure" and concurrent effects preserve valid work. Only secured stock should become fulfillment-ready, and cancellation must release only stock actually held.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: an expired order confirmed concurrently with admin work is exposed as fulfillment-ready before stock is held. For a concrete witness, current product stock is 0 (sold to another buyer); mark_paid writes placed, admin cancels and adds 1 stock, then mark_paid's _reserve consumes that 1 and increments sold. Final order is cancelled but its unit has been removed from sellable stock again. Alternatively packing can begin for stock that the later reserve fails to obtain. This violates inventory conservation and exposes paid orders that cannot safely be fulfilled; ordinary UI actions cannot reconcile the lost inventory automatically. This is a source-predicted interleaving, not an executed race.
reproduction_steps: Create an unpaid one-unit order, expire/release its reservation, and sell that unit to another buyer.
Complete the original payment late.
While verify/reconcile is between its order update and product reserve, cancel that now-visible Placed order from admin Orders.
Source trace predicts the cancellation restores a unit that mark_paid immediately reserves again despite the terminal cancelled order.
item.title: A late-paid order can be packed or cancelled before inventory is secured — mark_paid publishes placed before re-reserving

item.evidence: backend/routes_orders.py:99-105 sets a late-paid unavailable order to cancelled with refund_due; :210-211 returns {ok: True, status: fresh['status']}. frontend/src/pages/Checkout.jsx:85 discards that response and :86-88 clears the basket and toasts 'Payment successful — your order is placed!'.
item.expected: R-102: "the customer's order screen shows that recorded state"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "labels ... visible feedback ... against the actual operation state". Checkout must communicate paid-but-cancelled/refund-due rather than successful placement and preserve a reasonable recovery path.

The destination detail does explain cancellation, so the customer can discover the truth there, but receives contradictory success feedback and loses the saved basket needed to shop again.
reproduction_steps: Keep a Razorpay payment pending beyond reservation expiry.
Have the released stock purchased by another customer.
Complete the original payment so verify records cancelled/refund_due.
Source predicts the placed-success toast and cleared basket before the cancelled detail renders.
item.title: Late-paying shoppers are told their cancelled order was placed successfully — checkout ignores verify's returned status

item.evidence: backend/routes_orders.py:160 reserves products before provider creation. The try/except at :167-175 covers only Razorpay creation. The order insert at :177-185 is outside it; expiry at :128 can only find persisted orders.
item.expected: R-100 ties reservation to "the moment the order is created"; R-101 requires released unpaid reservations; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Multi-document operations leave no half-written state on failure". Subsequent expiry or abandon cannot restore them. This is a conditional source prediction; inventory repair requires admin intervention and the user's retry is a new checkout.
reproduction_steps: Start a configured checkout for one unit.
Let the provider create its order, then let the following local order insert fail.
Retry or wait past 15 minutes: source predicts the first hold has no persisted order and remains deducted.

item.evidence: backend/routes_orders.py:80-85 changes pending_payment/stock_reserved True to expired or abandoned/False, then runs _release, whose per-product writes are :73-75. item.expected: R-101: abandon/expiry "return the reserved quantity ... exactly once"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Multi-document operations leave no half-written state on failure". Release progress must be atomic or recoverable so each line is restored once even after interruption.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: with a two-product order, a connection/write failure after the first restored product leaves the other product deducted although the order is already terminal and claims no held stock. Neither retry nor future expiry can complete the missing release. The admin/customer receives failure but has no in-app safe retry to repair inventory. This is a source-backed failure-boundary prediction, independent of duplicate requests, which the compare-and-set correctly rejects.
reproduction_steps: Create an unpaid reservation containing two different products.
Dismiss payment or trigger expiry.
Let restoration of the second product fail after the order's terminal flag and first restoration commit.
Repeat abandon/expiry: source predicts the second quantity is never returned.
item.title: Expired or cancelled stock can be lost forever after a release write fails — cleanup marks the order released before restoring products

item.evidence: frontend/src/pages/admin/ProductDialog.jsx:79 labels an absolute 'Stock quantity'; frontend/src/pages/admin/AdminProducts.jsx:30 sends expected_stock from the opened product. backend/routes_admin.py:195-197 increments stock by stock - expected_stock without comparing the stored stock or version.

item.observed: Business logic and calculations: two admins both open stock 10, each enters Stock quantity 12 and saves. Each request adds 2, leaving 14 despite both intending to set the same inventory to 12. Sold goods need not exist for the extra units; subsequent checkout can accept phantom inventory. Admins can correct by recounting/re-editing, but receive success with materially misleading stock. Source prediction, not an executed concurrency test.
reproduction_steps: Open the same product (stock 10) in two admin sessions.
In each Edit product dialog enter Stock quantity 12.
Save both; read back inventory, which source predicts will be 14.
item.title: Two admins setting the same stock quantity silently inflate inventory — absolute edits are replayed as additive deltas

item.evidence: backend/routes_orders.py:217-218 marks a not-yet-captured dismissed payment abandoned; :128 scans only pending_payment/stock_reserved True, excluding abandoned/expired orders. :224-228 reconciles only three newest unpaid orders from 48 hours. :229-230 returns only locally paid orders. frontend/src/pages/Orders.jsx:35-51 exposes only those returned orders; no webhook route is registered in backend/server.py:29-33 or routes_orders.py.
item.expected: R-102 requires late confirmed payments to be recorded as reserved/paid or refund-due; checklist, Third-party integrations: "an accepted asynchronous request is not a finished operation" and delayed dependency outcomes must reach visible status/recovery. Captured money must be reconciled even when a browser closed or newer checkout attempts exist.
item.observed: Payments and billing: if Razorpay captures an abandoned order after its last reconciliation (for example delayed confirmation), then the user creates three newer unpaid attempts, My orders never examines the captured older order. The expiry scan excludes it and there is no webhook/background reconciliation. My orders filters it out as locally unpaid, leaving the customer charged with no fulfillment/refund record or reachable order link. After 48 hours the same omission applies even without newer attempts. Admin viewing the unpaid list also does not reconcile abandoned entries. Recovery requires access to the hidden order id or developer/manual provider investigation; it is not an ordinary in-app recovery. This is conditional source evidence, not an observed provider capture.
reproduction_steps: Start payment A and dismiss it while Razorpay still reports no captured payment; abandon releases its stock.
Let Razorpay confirm/capture A later, without the browser success handler verifying it.
Create and abandon three newer checkouts before visiting My orders (or return more than 48 hours later).
Open My orders and admin Orders: source predicts A stays locally unpaid and absent from the customer's list indefinitely.
item.surface: Late Razorpay completion; GET /api/orders; abandoned-payment recovery
item.title: Customers can be charged without an order or refund state appearing — late-payment reconciliation silently skips older abandoned checkouts

item.evidence: backend/routes_admin.py:294-296 checks the current admin count before a demotion, then :297 performs the change separately. :298-299 restores the request's target to admin whenever the later count is zero, regardless of that target's original or requested role. Keeping an admin must not unexpectedly grant admin authority to a customer being assigned delivery access.

If C's post-update count runs while both admins are demoted, the unconditional fallback promotes C to admin. The demotion requests can then observe C as the remaining admin and return success. C receives full inventory, customer/order and role-management authority although the approved action granted only delivery. This is a source-predicted race, not an executed privilege escalation.
reproduction_steps: Have exactly two admin accounts and customer C.
In concurrently authorized requests, demote both admins and change C's role to delivery.
Interleave the two demotion writes before C's post-update admin-count check, and C's fallback before the demotion checks.
Source predicts C becomes admin while both intended admins become customers.
item.title: A customer being made a rider can unexpectedly become the only admin — last-admin compensation promotes any request target

item.evidence: backend/routes_ai.py:36-41 breaks on StreamDone but does not remember receiving it. R-108 preserves an in-flight reply, and inherited R-016/R-078 require its full text, not a silently finalized partial buffer.

The shopper receives no cutoff indication and sees the truncated answer as final after reload; admin insights use the same helper. Asking again can recover the task, but the existing incomplete advice is misrepresented as complete. This conclusion is conditional on the specified stream event sequence, not a claim about observed model behavior.
reproduction_steps: Send a shopping question or Generate insights.
At the integration boundary, let the stream yield one or more TextDelta events and then end without StreamDone.
Source predicts a synthetic done event and, for chat, persisted partial content with no cutoff warning.

Sign out and sign in as account B in the same SPA.
Allow B's /me response to finish, then the old A response to arrive.
Open checkout with items and no prefilled address: source predicts A's saved delivery details populate B's form.

item.title: A new account can see the previous shopper's saved address — delayed account fetches survive sign-out and overwrite current state

item.evidence: backend/routes_admin.py:95 caps the order list at 300 with no offset/cursor/total; frontend/src/pages/admin/AdminOrders.jsx:95-128 offers filters/search and renders the array but no next page or truncation warning. frontend/src/pages/Shop.jsx:44 requests limit 200 and :91-93 renders only those rows; backend/routes_store.py:42,52 caps the result and exposes no pagination/total.
item.expected: Request: "all the grocery items"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "pagination reaches the last page ... exposes truncation". Inherited R-076 requires every matching product exactly once across pages; admins likewise need complete order access as data grows.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: with 201 matching active products, Shop shows only 200 and labels that truncated count as the item total; with 301 matching paid orders, admin Orders silently omits the oldest one. Neither screen can page to the missing rows. Searching a known exact name/order number can recover particular records, but discovery and complete review require manual filter/search partitioning, which is meaningful extra work. The limits are source-proven; no latency measurement is claimed.
reproduction_steps: Populate more than 200 active products and open All groceries.
Observe the source-predicted 200-item list with no next page or disclosure.
With more than 300 paid orders, open All paid orders in admin Orders.
The oldest matching order is omitted with no way to page to it.
item.title: Shoppers and admins cannot browse the full catalogue or order history — list limits silently truncate results without pagination

item.evidence: backend/routes_admin.py:95 returns the first 300 sorted matching orders with no cursor/offset/total. frontend/src/pages/admin/AdminOrders.jsx:95-128 supplies search/filter and renders only the returned array, with no paging control or truncation notice.
item.expected: R-088: "admin order list ... by paging rather than returning everything"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "pagination reaches the last page ... exposes truncation". With 301 paid orders, an admin must be able to reach the oldest matching order without knowing its number first.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: after 300 matching paid orders, older orders disappear from admin browsing. Searching a known order number may retrieve one, but there is no way to review the complete history or discover an old cancellation/refund case by paging. Admins must manually partition searches/filters, and a large single-status population still remains truncated. This is a source-predicted growth boundary, not a measured performance claim.

Open All paid orders in admin Orders.
Source predicts only the newest 300 appear with no next page.
Try the same status filter: the oldest order still cannot be reached by paging.
item.title: Admins cannot browse older matching orders after 300 records — the list has a hard cap but no pagination

item.evidence: backend/routes_admin.py:228-229 atomically changes application pending to approved through _claim_application; :245 commits that claim before :247-248 updates the user role/profile. A failure in that user update is not compensated or retried. _claim_application at :230-233 refuses a second approval because the application is no longer pending.
item.expected: Request: "They sign up, admin approves"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Multi-document operations leave no half-written state on failure". Approval must grant the rider role/profile or remain recoverably pending, rather than permanently consume the approval action first.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: if the user-role write fails after the application claim commits, admin sees an error but reloading lists the application as approved while the applicant still has customer access. Repeating Approve returns 409, so the approval workflow cannot repair itself and the rider cannot open deliveries. Admin can manually change the role in Users & roles, but that does not reproduce the missing rider-profile write; this is bounded administrative recovery work, not successful approval. Conditional source prediction, not a simulated database failure.
reproduction_steps: Submit a pending delivery-partner application.
As admin click Approve.
Let the application update succeed but the subsequent user update fail.
Reload and retry approval: source predicts approved application, customer role, and a 409 on retry.
item.title: Applicants can remain customers after being marked approved — approval commits before the role/profile write and cannot be retried

item.evidence: frontend/src/pages/ProductDetail.jsx:28 handles every product GET rejection with setMissing(True); :32-33 displays 'This product is not available' and only Back to shop. There is no distinction for network errors/500 versus actual 404.
item.expected: Request: "everything should be clear"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "Resolve ... failure ... against the actual operation state"; R-068 requires failed fetches to show an error rather than a real empty/unavailable result. A service outage should be reported as a loading failure with a usable recovery path, not a claim the product is unavailable.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: shoppers opening an in-stock product during a transient network/server failure are told that product is unavailable. They cannot retry on the page and may abandon an item that is actually purchasable. Reload or returning from Shop after connectivity recovers can restore it, so the impairment is bounded but misleading.
reproduction_steps: Open an existing in-stock product while its GET request fails with 500 or a network error.
Read the product page's result.
Source predicts 'This product is not available' instead of a fetch error/retry.
item.title: Shoppers are falsely told stocked products are unavailable during outages — detail treats every fetch failure as a missing product

item.evidence: frontend/src/pages/admin/AdminProducts.jsx:21 catches inventory fetch failures with setProducts([]); :48 converts that to an empty list, :52 reports '0 products in catalog', and :72-86 renders no rows or failure message/retry.
item.expected: R-068: "a failed fetch shows an error rather than an empty table"; request: "everything should be clear". An inventory request failure must not be presented as a real empty store.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: when the inventory request fails, an admin sees an apparently empty catalogue and a zero count instead of the store's actual stock. They cannot distinguish outage from lost products or retry in place, creating unnecessary investigation and potential duplicate restocking work. Reload after connectivity returns is a safe recovery, but the displayed zero is false.
reproduction_steps: Open Products as admin while GET /api/admin/products fails.
Inspect the catalogue count and rows.
Source predicts 0 products and an empty table without an error or Retry.
item.title: Admins see a false empty catalogue after inventory fetch failure — error handler replaces products with an empty array
